methodology.positives: The original three URLScan-observed stores per rule are all treated as development data because rule authors saw them. After the rules and same-resource two-signal policy were frozen, a separate 119-page public holdout was sealed with two or three non-development stores per rule. Failed holdout rows remain in the metric and were not used to retune rules.
methodology.negatives: Forty controlled hostname-only hard negatives share each vendor domain while omitting the independent pathname and body markers required by the rule.
methodology.scope: Engineering fixture gate only; these rates do not claim population-wide coverage.

limitations: Server-side integrations and strict-sandbox Web Pixels can be invisible to main-page resource collection.
A public-browser signal match is not proof of installation ownership, event delivery, traffic, or sales volume.
